about.title: Williams Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Williams is a small Colusa County community, but its roads carry heavy regional traffic — Rt 20 and I-5 bring through-travelers and freight past local intersections at E Street and 8th Street every day. Recent public records show 10 injury collisions and 14 injured people in a single year, with a concentration of reported crashes on Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m., likely tied to end-of-week commuting and highway merges. When a collision happens here, the aftermath can be disorienting: medical visits, vehicle repairs, missed work, and calls from insurance adjusters all at once. We handle personal injury claims arising from car accidents in Colusa County. Our team can review your situation, explain your options, and help you avoid early missteps that could affect your claim. There's no cost for a consultation, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a road agency along Rt 20 or I-5 — is involved. We can flag this early so you don't lose your right to file.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Shift Blame Onto You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning any percentage of blame assigned to you reduces your recovery. Insurers know this and often push recorded statements to get you to say something that shifts fault their way.

items.title: No Cap Means Your Full Story Matters
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so a thorough case record matters. We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover, so getting your case reviewed costs you nothing upfront.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use these statements to look for ways to reduce or deny a claim, and casual wording can be taken out of context. We can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my crash happened on I-5 or Rt 20 and involved a state or county road issue?
items.answer: If a government entity's road design, signage, or maintenance played a role, California law can require a much shorter filing deadline — sometimes just six months. Given how much of Williams' reported crash activity happens on I-5 and Rt 20, it's worth having us check this quickly rather than waiting.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer a free consultation, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward after the initial conversation.
